concepts.title: Biosphere, Ecosystem and Ecological Balance
concepts.definition: The biosphere is the narrow zone where lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere meet and life exists, organised into ecosystems of producers, consumers and decomposers exchanging energy and matter through food chains, food webs and nutrient cycling, which keep the ecological balance.
concepts.key_idea: Energy flows one way through the ecosystem from green plants to consumers, while nutrients recycle, so disruption at any level unbalances the whole system.

concepts.title: Biodiversity, Its Loss and Conservation
concepts.definition: Biodiversity covers the variety of genes, species and ecosystems on the earth, and its loss proceeds through habitat destruction, overexploitation, pollution, invasive species and climate change, demanding conservation through biosphere reserves, national parks, sanctuaries and laws.
concepts.key_idea: Tropical forests hold the richest biodiversity, and in-situ conservation in reserves alongside ex-situ methods like zoos and gene banks protects species for the future.

concepts.title: Life Forms, Their Evolution and Threats to the Biosphere
concepts.definition: Life evolved in the primordial oceans from simple cells to complex plants and animals over billions of years, and today pollution, habitat loss, invasive species and climate change threaten the biosphere, so environmental ethics and sustainable living are needed to keep the earth habitable.
concepts.key_idea: Human survival depends on the biosphere's services of oxygen, food, water purification and climate regulation, which damaged ecosystems can no longer provide.
